description: Send email from the connected Gmail account, governed: counted against a limit, held for approval when a policy says so, and receipted. Anlyon can send only; it cannot read the mailbox.

secrets.name: GMAIL
secrets.description: The connected Gmail account the agent sends from

actions.name: send-email
actions.description: Send one email from the connected Gmail account. raw is the whole message in RFC 2822 form (From, To, Cc, Subject and the other headers, a blank line, then the body), base64url-encoded. Google sends it to every address in its To, Cc and Bcc headers and keeps a copy in Sent. Returns the message id and thread id. Counted as one email per call, whatever the number of recipients. No read-back: Anlyon asks Google only for permission to send (gmail.send), and every permission that could read a message back would let it read the mailbox, so the receipt is graded acknowledged, the same grade an adopted MCP tool gets. Limitation: an approval shows raw as it was given, so decode it before approving. Limitation: no idempotency, so a retry after an unknown outcome can send the email twice. Limitation: raw is at most 4,096 characters, about 3 KB of message, so no attachments.

raw.description: The RFC 2822 message, base64url-encoded (the URL-safe alphabet, - and _, padding optional). Its headers name the recipients and the subject; From may be left out, and Google sets it to the connected account.

thread_id.description: Send as a reply in this thread: a threadId an earlier send-email returned. The message's Subject must match the thread's, and its In-Reply-To and References headers should name the message replied to.
